source_natively_supported_prescreen.evidence: Environment supplies task-specific reward and response-cost consequences; EVC/metareasoning computes normative relative value and Q of selecting control specifications, separate from external reward and measured human behavior.

Approximate learned value of control LVOC(s,c) combines feature weights f_k(s), control intensity c_l, feature-control interactions, intrinsic cost(c) and latency cost wT; linear/additive approximation is a model assumption.
Approximate posterior learning of w from actual experience e_t=(state,control,reward,time,next state); complete detailed deferred-credit math is S1 and currently not verified.

Posterior sampling averaged weight draw selects high estimated value control; stopping/selection bound derives from expected cost of computation or reward-rate optimization, not independent evidence that the brain implements exact sampler.

source_natively_supported_prescreen.locator: main model variants and behavioral simulation sections
source_natively_supported_prescreen.evidence: Compared simulated LVOC predictions against published prior human visual attention and Stroop/Flanker data and alternatives RW associative and WSLS; source simulation comparison is not new participant observation or direct neural proof.

Incorrect feature linearity predicts maladaptive overexertion for nonlinear context, and source identifies other required extensions (e.g. change point/discount factors and control sequences) as future work rather than tested baseline.
